svg.text: Same lap, same grip, half the tire

Each wheel's friction circle — the ring is everything that tire has at that instant, the fill is how much of it is being spent. Both variants reach the apex at the same grip and get round in the same time. What differs is what they spend on the straight afterwards.
at the apex
Hardest cornering. Both variants are near the limit;
there is almost nothing to choose between them here.
variant H — RL Mz + allocator
seed 0
average 87% of grip in use
variant E — end-to-end
seed 2
average 98% of grip in use
on the exit straight
Going in a straight line. H has let the tires go; E
is still spending most of what they have.
average 17% of grip in use
average 51% of grip in use
Averaged over the whole lap, H spends 36% of the available grip and E spends 70% — and the three seeds of each do not overlap. They get round in the
same time and reach the same peak cornering force while doing it, so this is not H driving more slowly.
The gap is not in the corner. It is on the straight, which is 260 of this lap's 393 m. Why is not settled: H's allocator will happily produce
opposing wheel forces on a straight if its policy asks for a yaw moment there, and on some seeds it does.
[MEASURED] friction-ellipse utilisation = hypot(Fx/Fx_peak, Fy/Fy_peak) per wheel, deployed policy, representative seed (median finish distance) · RUNG 2 (rule 15)
Arrow direction inside each circle is where that tire's force points; length and percentage are how much of its capacity is spent.
